questions.question: What LGE pattern is characteristic of a myocardial infarction (ischemic disease)?
choices: C. Subendocardial or transmural enhancement in a coronary territory
questions.detail: Ischemic injury always begins in the subendocardium and spreads outward (the 'wavefront' phenomenon).

questions.question: In the setting of an acute MI, an area of 'no-reflow' (dark core within a bright LGE area) represents:
questions.detail: MVO represents capillary destruction; it is a poor prognostic sign indicating the tissue is non-viable despite revascularization.

questions.question: Which term describes myocardium that has decreased contractility due to CHRONIC ischemia but remains viable?
questions.detail: Hibernating myocardium is a state of adaptive down-regulation; it is viable and will recover function after revascularization.

questions.question: 'Stunned myocardium' refers to:
choices: A. Chronic ischemia causing permanent scar
B. Temporary dysfunction following ACUTE ischemia and successful reperfusion
C. Dead tissue that enhances on LGE
questions.detail: Stunned tissue is dysfunctional but viable and will eventually recover without further intervention.

questions.question: Post-infarction Dressler syndrome is characterized by:
choices: C. Late-onset pericarditis, pleuritis, and fever
questions.detail: Dressler syndrome is an autoimmune-mediated pericarditis occurring weeks to months after an MI.

questions.question: A 'true' ventricular aneurysm differs from a 'pseudoaneurysm' in that a true aneurysm:
choices: A. Has a wide neck and involves all layers of the heart wall
B. Has a narrow neck and is prone to rupture
C. Is caused by bacterial infection
E. Only occurs in the right ventricle
questions.detail: True aneurysms have a wide neck and are generally lower risk for rupture than pseudoaneurysms, which have narrow necks.

questions.question: Thallium-201 'rest-redistribution' imaging is used to identify:
questions.detail: Uptake on delayed redistribution images indicates viable cells that can be saved with surgery.

questions.question: A 'fixed' defect on a Tc-99m sestamibi SPECT perfusion scan (seen on both stress and rest) represents:
questions.detail: A fixed defect implies the tissue is not taking up tracer normally at rest, suggesting it is either scarred or hibernating.

questions.question: 'Transient Ischemic Dilation' (TID) on a stress perfusion scan is a marker of:
choices: B. Left main or three-vessel coronary artery disease
questions.detail: TID represents diffuse subendocardial ischemia and indicates a worse prognosis.

questions.question: Which of the following is a classic mechanical complication occurring 3–7 days after a large MI?
questions.detail: Myocardial necrosis can lead to septal rupture (VSD) or papillary muscle rupture in the first week post-MI.

questions.question: 'Microvascular obstruction' (MVO) is best identified on CMR using:
choices: B. Early (first-pass) or early LGE images (1–2 minutes)
questions.detail: MVO appears as a central dark zone of non-enhancement within the bright infarcted area.

questions.question: Myocardial 'viability' on CMR is best predicted by the:
choices: A. Thickness of the LGE (transmural extent)
questions.detail: Segments with <50% transmural enhancement are likely to recover function after revascularization.
